# Trading Brief — 2026-08-04

# Section 3: Horizon Scan — Regulatory & Catalyst Events

_Scan run: 2026-08-04 07:00 CT (12:00 UTC)_

---

## 1. DEA Marijuana Rescheduling — ALJ Recommendation Imminent

**Event Type:** P1 — Regulatory decision (Schedule I → III)
**Future Catalyst Date:** ALJ recommendation window ~Sept–Oct 2026; DEA Administrator final ruling ~Q4 2026–Q1 2027
**Time Remaining:** ~4–8 weeks to ALJ recommendation

**What happened:** The DEA's formal evidentiary hearing on marijuana rescheduling concluded July 15, 2026 after two and a half weeks of testimony. Chief ALJ Derek Julius ordered post-hearing briefs due **August 17, 2026** (50-page max). After receiving briefs, the ALJ will write his recommended decision — no timeline specified, but historically this takes 4–12 weeks. The final call rests with DEA Administrator Terrance Cole. Medical marijuana is already temporarily Schedule III under a separate April 2026 acting AG order; this hearing addresses comprehensive rescheduling of all marijuana.

**Why it matters:** This is the closest federal cannabis reform has ever gotten to the finish line. The ALJ recommendation is the last procedural gate before a final rule. If the ALJ recommends rescheduling (likely given DEA/FDA testimony emphasized medical benefit and relative safety), the Administrator faces enormous political pressure to act. Cannabis stocks are deeply depressed — MSOS trades at $4.21, down 42% from its $7.25 52-week high. The asymmetry is significant: a favorable recommendation could trigger a multi-week rerating across the sector, while an unfavorable one keeps the status quo (medical already rescheduled). Note: only opponents were allowed to participate as designated parties, which introduces uncertainty, but the underlying scientific record strongly favors rescheduling.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | Price (8/3) | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| MSOS | $4.21 | US cannabis ETF (multi-operator) | Purest proxy for rescheduling sentiment; leveraged to federal reform |
| CGC | $0.96 | Canopy Growth — cannabis producer | Balance sheet survival contingent on rescheduling unlocking US plant-touching |
| TLRY | $4.64 | Tilray — cannabis + alcohol | Optionality on rescheduling + diversification into adjacents |

**What would prove this wrong:** ALJ recommends against rescheduling (unlikely given hearing record); litigation in D.C. Circuit stays the process indefinitely; Administrator declines to follow recommendation. Political risk: a public health crisis narrative could override the regulatory process.

**If this plays out:** MSOS could see 30–60% upside over 2–4 weeks on a favorable ALJ recommendation, with further upside on final rule. CGC/TLRY have more idiosyncratic risk but offer higher beta. Schedule III unlocks 280E tax relief (deductible business expenses) — a massive earnings catalyst for plant-touching operators.

**Key signals to watch:**
- August 17: post-hearing brief deadline (parties' final arguments)
- ALJ recommended decision publication (likely Sept–Oct)
- D.C. Circuit litigation status (consolidated appeals could stay the rule)
- DEA Administrator public statements

**Sources:**
- [Marijuana Moment](https://www.marijuanamoment.net/federal-marijuana-rescheduling-hearing-wraps-up-with-dea-judge-laying-out-next-steps/) — confirms Aug 17 brief deadline, ALJ process, no timeline for recommendation
- [DEA Official Page](https://www.dea.gov/marijuana-rescheduling-regulatory-actions) — confirms hearing dates (June 29–July 15), participant selection, prior rescheduling actions
- [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/dc-circuit-challenge-dea-hearing-put-federal-cannabis-rescheduling-test--pracin-2026-07-08/) — confirms D.C. Circuit litigation overhang

---

## 2. Compass Pathways COMP360 — First-Ever Psychedelic NDA Approaching

**Event Type:** P1 — FDA drug approval decision
**Future Catalyst Date:** NDA completion ~Q3 2026; approval decision Q4 2026–Q1 2027 (CNPV-accelerated 1–2 month review)
**Time Remaining:** ~8–20 weeks to approval decision

**What happened:** Compass Pathways (CMPS) is conducting a rolling NDA submission for COMP360 (synthetic psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression), supported by two positive Phase 3 trials. FDA granted a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) on April 24, 2026 under EO 14401, targeting a 1–2 month review post-submission. The 26-week durability data from COMP006 Part B read out positive on July 7, 2026 — the final clinical gating item. Rolling NDA modules are being submitted; final submission expected Q3 2026. Compass confirmed "launch ready by end of 2026."

**Why it matters:** This would be the first classic psychedelic ever approved by the FDA. The CNPV program's track record: Eli Lilly's orforglipron was approved in 50 days under CNPV. If COMP360 follows a similar timeline, approval could come as early as Q4 2026. The market is not pricing this well — CMPS trades at $11.24, down 27% from its $15.40 June high (profit-taking after initial EO enthusiasm). ~90% of the US population lives in states that intend to reschedule COMP360 within 30 days of FDA approval. The total addressable market for TRD is ~2.8M patients in the US alone.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | Price (8/3) | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| CMPS | $11.24 | Compass Pathways — psilocybin developer | Pure-play on COMP360 approval; ~$1.5B market cap vs multi-billion TAM |
| NVO | $47.09 | Novo Nordisk (reference) | CNPV precedent (orforglipron) validates the pathway; not directly impacted |

**What would prove this wrong:** FDA convenes an Advisory Committee (as happened with Lykos/MDMA in 2024 — a disaster); CNPV review timeline slips beyond 2 months; REMS requirements make commercial viability questionable; DEA rescheduling of psilocybin doesn't proceed in parallel as EO 14401 contemplates.

**If this plays out:** CMPS could 2–3x on approval given small float (129M shares), zero revenue currently, and transformational nature of first-mover advantage in psychedelic medicine. REMS requirements will create a service-center model that could generate $2–5K+ per treatment session.

**Key signals to watch:**
- NDA final submission completion (expected Q3 2026 — watch for company announcement)
- FDA filing acceptance letter (triggers CNPV review clock)
- Any AdCom announcement (would be negative signal — suggests FDA has concerns)
- DEA parallel rescheduling initiation under EO 14401 §5
- Compass quarterly updates on commercial preparedness

**Sources:**
- [Psilocybin FDA Approval Tracker — Psychedelic Beacon](https://psychedelicbeacon.com/blog/psilocybin-fda-approval-tracker) — comprehensive timeline, CNPV mechanics, NDA status
- [Compass IR — CNPV Award](https://ir.compasspathways.com/News--Events-/news/news-details/2026/Compass-Pathways-Announces-FDA-Granted-NDA-Rolling-Review-Request-and-Awarded-Commissioners-National-Priority-Voucher/default.aspx) — confirms CNPV, rolling NDA
- [Compass IR — Phase 3 Durability](https://ir.compasspathways.com/News--Events-/news/news-details/2026/Compass-Pathways-Announces-Six-Month-Data-from-Second-Phase-3-Trial-Confirming-Rapid-and-Durable-Profile/default.aspx) — confirms six-month data, H1 2027 launch target
- [EO 14401 — White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/04/accelerating-medical-treatments-for-serious-mental-illness/) — directive prioritizing psychedelic review

---

## 3. GLP-1 Compounding — FDA Final Decision on 503B Exclusion Pending

**Event Type:** P1 — FDA regulatory final decision
**Future Catalyst Date:** Imminent — comment period closed June 30, 2026; final decision could drop any time
**Time Remaining:** 0–8 weeks (overdue window)

**What happened:** On April 30, 2026, FDA proposed removing semaglutide, tirzepatide, and liraglutide from the 503B Bulks List — which would prohibit outsourcing facilities from compounding these GLP-1 drugs. The public comment period closed June 30, 2026. FDA is now reviewing comments and is expected to issue a final decision. This would effectively end the compounded GLP-1 gray market that emerged during shortage periods. Separately, the national shortage has been declared over, removing the 503B shortage exemption independent of the bulks list action.

**Why it matters:** This is a binary regulatory event with direct, material impact on both sides. For branded manufacturers (LLY, NVO), it eliminates compounded competition and consolidates pricing power. For telehealth compounders (HIMS sells compounded GLP-1s), it removes a significant revenue stream. HIMS has already been crushed — down 53% from its $65.59 52-week high — but compounded GLP-1 revenue remains a material portion of its growth narrative. The decision could come at any time with no scheduled announcement date, creating an asymmetric options setup.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | Price (8/3) | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| LLY | $1,121.36 | Eli Lilly — tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) | Positive: removes compounded competitors, defends pricing |
| NVO | $47.09 | Novo Nordisk — semaglutide (Wegovy/Ozempic) | Positive: same dynamic |
| HIMS | $30.82 | Hims & Hers — telehealth, sells compounded GLP-1s | Negative: loses a high-margin revenue line |

**What would prove this wrong:** FDA reverses course and keeps GLP-1s on the 503B list (unlikely given shortage is over and FDA proposed the removal); further litigation from compounders delays enforcement; HIMS has already pivoted to other product lines, minimizing impact.

**If this plays out:** Branded GLP-1 manufacturers get a modest tailwind (mostly priced in, but enforcement removes the discount-driven channel). HIMS faces a revenue cliff for its weight loss program — could see 10–20% downside on the announcement. The key asymmetry is on the HIMS short side or LLY/NVO long side.

**Key signals to watch:**
- FDA Federal Register notice publishing final rule on 503B bulks list
- HIRS/HIMS earnings commentary on GLP-1 revenue concentration
- Warning letters to 503B outsourcing facilities still compounding GLP-1s
- State pharmacy board enforcement actions

**Sources:**
- [Pharmacy Times](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/fda-moves-to-permanently-close-the-door-on-compounded-glp-1s) — confirms proposal, comment period
- [Lachman Consultants](https://www.lachmanconsultants.com/2026/05/preliminary-decision-to-exclude-certain-glp-1-drugs-from-the-503b-bulks-list/) — confirms June 30 comment deadline
- [Medical News Today](https://www.medicalnewstoday.com/articles/fda-proposes-ban-bulk-compounding-semaglutide-tirzepatide) — confirms three drugs proposed for exclusion

---

## 4. DEA Telemedicine Controlled Substance Prescribing — Permanent Rule Overdue

**Event Type:** P2 — Regulatory cliff
**Future Catalyst Date:** December 31, 2026 (4th temporary extension expires); permanent rule could be proposed any time
**Time Remaining:** ~5 months to cliff

**What happened:** The DEA has now issued four temporary extensions of COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities allowing prescribing of Schedule II–V controlled substances without prior in-person evaluation. The current extension runs through December 31, 2026. The DEA has been "working on" a permanent rule since 2023 but has not proposed one. Each extension has been narrower in scope, signaling the DEA intends to eventually restrict telemedicine prescribing. A permanent proposed rule could drop at any time.

**Why it matters:** Telehealth platforms (HIMS, teladoc-type models) have built business models partly on these flexibilities. A restrictive permanent rule would curtail remote prescribing of controlled medications — impacting ADHD treatment, TRT, anxiety meds, and opioid recovery programs. The market is not pricing this cliff because extensions have become routine. But the DEA is under political pressure from both sides: patient access advocates want permanence; DEA diversion control hawks want restrictions. The asymmetry: if a restrictive rule drops, telehealth stocks face immediate revaluation.

**Direct-impact tickers:**

| Ticker | Price (8/3) | What it does | Why it moves |
|--------|------------|-------------|--------------|
| HIMS | $30.82 | Hims & Hers — telehealth platform | Direct exposure: controlled substance prescribing is material to several product lines |

**What would prove this wrong:** Fifth temporary extension (kicks the can again — base case given DEA's track record); permanent rule is permissive and codifies current flexibilities.

**If this plays out:** Telehealth names with controlled-substance revenue concentration face 15–30% drawdowns on a restrictive rule. Combined with GLP-1 compounding decision (above), HIMS faces a potential double-whammy.

**Key signals to watch:**
- DEA Federal Register notices on telemedicine
- HHS/DEA joint statements on permanent rule timeline
- Congressional pressure or hearing scheduling on telemedicine prescribing
- December 31, 2026 approaching with no action = fifth extension likely

**Sources:**
- [Federal Register — Fourth Extension](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/31/2025-24123/fourth-temporary-extension-of-covid-19-telemedicine-flexibilities-for-prescription-of-controlled) — confirms Dec 31, 2026 expiration
- [McDermott Law](https://www.mcdermottlaw.com/insights/dea-telemedicine-flexibilities-for-controlled-substances-2026/) — confirms permanent rule still unwritten

---

_Scan complete. Next run: 2026-08-05 07:00 CT._
